contents.name: Applications to Cell Complexes
contents.reason: The source's remaining results use cell attachment and skeleta, machinery deliberately assigned to the cellular-homology development.

contents.name: Fundamental-group presentations of closed orientable and nonorientable surfaces
contents.reason: The plan has no topological classification-of-surfaces page, and placing these presentation calculations needs an owner decision rather than an invented destination.

contents.name: Corollary 1.27: closed orientable surfaces of different genera are not homotopy equivalent
contents.reason: This genus-separation result depends on the surface presentations immediately preceding it, for which the present plan supplies no dedicated page.

contents.name: Corollary 1.28: every group is the fundamental group of a 2-dimensional cell complex
contents.reason: Realizing arbitrary presentations by 2-complexes uses the cell-attachment result and belongs with the planned construction of CW complexes.

sources.title: J. Peter May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

contents.name: Section 5: The classification of coverings of groupoids
contents.reason: The groupoid prototype requires the fundamental-groupoid and category interfaces ordered after this page; its connected space consequences are included below.

contents.name: Theorem: lifting criterion and uniqueness for a functor into a covering groupoid
contents.reason: This theorem is about functors between groupoids, whose objects and morphisms are not available at order 299; the topological lifting criterion is already published separately.

contents.name: Definition: a map of coverings of a groupoid
contents.reason: This is the groupoid analogue of the already-published topological covering morphism and needs the later fundamental-groupoid category interface.

contents.name: Lemma: a map of coverings of groupoids is itself a covering
contents.reason: The groupoid-covering lemma requires the deferred groupoid category; the scaffold proves the analogous topological covering-morphism statement directly from sheets.

contents.name: Theorem: maps of connected groupoid coverings correspond to subgroup inclusion; isomorphism corresponds to equality and unbased isomorphism to conjugacy
Corollary: a universal covering groupoid is unique and covers every other connected cover
contents.reason: The corollary is explicitly about universal covering groupoids; the topological universal-cover theorem is published, but it is not the same categorical object.

contents.name: Theorem: maps of coverings correspond to equivariant maps of fibres
contents.reason: The full equivariant-map correspondence is part of the disconnected categorical equivalence and is not needed for connected subgroup classification.

contents.name: Definition: automorphism group of a covering groupoid
contents.reason: Automorphisms of a covering groupoid require the later groupoid interface; deck transformations are the topological analogue, not an identical published definition.

contents.name: Section 6: The construction of coverings of groupoids
contents.reason: The orbit-category construction is the categorical model for arbitrary disconnected covers, whose formal prerequisites occur after order 299.

contents.name: Theorem: the orbit category of the fundamental group is equivalent to connected coverings of the groupoid
contents.reason: Equivalence of categories cannot be stated load-bearingly before the planned category-theory definitions, while the subgroup-by-subgroup space construction closes locally.

contents.name: Remark: equivalent descriptions by groupoid functors and fundamental-group sets
contents.reason: These equivalent categorical descriptions refine the disconnected theory and add no needed claim to the connected classification spine.

contents.name: Section 7: The classification of coverings of spaces
Fundamental theorem of covering space theory: lift existence and uniqueness from subgroup inclusion
Definition: a map of coverings over a fixed base space
Lemma: a map of connected coverings is itself a covering
Theorem: a based covering morphism exists exactly under subgroup inclusion and is unique; equality and conjugacy classify isomorphism
Corollary: the fundamental groupoid functor gives a bijection on covering morphisms
contents.reason: This formal fundamental-groupoid statement needs the later groupoid item; the underlying topological morphism criterion is proved directly here.

contents.name: Theorem: covering morphisms correspond to fundamental-group-equivariant fibre maps
contents.reason: The all-coverings equivariant-map theorem is a categorical refinement beyond the connected subgroup and normalizer results required by this page.

contents.name: Definition: automorphism group of a covering
Corollary: the automorphism group is the subgroup normalizer quotient, with regular and universal special cases
Section 8: The construction of coverings of spaces
Construction of the universal cover from endpoint-fixed path classes
Definition: a G-space and its orbit space
Lemma: passage to subgroup orbit spaces is functorial
contents.reason: Functoriality over the orbit category belongs to the deferred categorical equivalence; one fixed subgroup quotient is all the connected realization proof uses.

contents.name: Proposition: a cover with fibre-transitive automorphism group is regular and its automorphism orbit space is the base
Theorem: subgroup orbit spaces of the universal cover define an orbit-category equivalence with connected coverings
contents.reason: The subgroup-realization clause is included locally, but the theorem's equivalence-of-categories assertion requires categorical interfaces ordered after this page.

contents.name: Construction of general connected covers as subgroup orbit spaces of the universal cover
Corollary: the fundamental-groupoid functor is an equivalence between coverings of a space and coverings of its groupoid
contents.reason: This corollary is a formal groupoid equivalence and cannot be stated before the later fundamental-groupoid and category-equivalence definitions.

contents.name: Problem 1: lift the group multiplication to a covering of a connected locally path-connected topological group
contents.reason: Lifting a topological-group structure is a theorem about topological groups, an additional subject not developed by this page's declared covering-space prerequisites.

contents.name: Problem 2: the covering kernel is discrete, normal, central, and identifies with the automorphism group
contents.reason: The kernel and centrality assertions depend on the lifted topological-group multiplication from Problem 1 rather than on classification of coverings as spaces alone.

contents.name: Problem 3: a surjective local homeomorphism need not be a covering
Problem 4: a local homeomorphism with compact Hausdorff domain is a finite-sheeted covering of a connected Hausdorff target
Problem 5: equivariant maps from G/H to a G-space form the H-fixed-point space
contents.reason: The fixed-point mapping-space homeomorphism belongs to equivariant topology and is not used by the subgroup classification or normalizer quotient proved here.

contents.name: Problem 6: fixed-point spaces define a contravariant functor on the orbit category
contents.reason: This functorial fixed-point construction requires the deferred orbit-category interface and contributes no load-bearing fact to connected covering classification.
